title: Insights H1 2026 retro: our best work came from planned projects, but ad-hoc requests took almost half our time
subtitle: What the team shipped, which decisions it changed, what we learned, and what we will do differently in H2, starting with a single home for our work.
summary: In H1 2026 the nine-person Insights team published 12 pieces, supported 23 experiments and answered 312 ad-hoc requests. Most of the measurable impact came from planned work such as the checkout test and the carousel holdout. Ad-hoc work grew to 46% of team time, and 38% of those requests had already been answered somewhere, so H2 priorities are launching the Insights Hub, triaging intake and building a self-serve metric layer.
key_findings: 12 published pieces, 23 experiments supported and 312 ad-hoc requests in H1 with 9 FTE.
The checkout test and carousel holdout account for about $30M of annualised revenue acted on by leadership.
Ad-hoc work rose from 41% of team hours in Q1 to 46% in Q2.
38% of ad-hoc requests asked something already answered in an existing report, dashboard or definition.
Pre-registered tests reached a decision in a median of 6 days after readout, versus 19 days without.
